notebooks.title: Thermodynamic and Practical Costs of Memory Reliability
notebooks.summary: This provisional notebook explores the dual perspectives on memory cost: the theoretical necessity of distinct memory states for work production in information engines and the practical energy overhead imposed by refresh requirements in DRAM systems.
notebooks.findings:
In physical DRAM implementations, energy cost is directly tied to retention time through periodic refresh mechanisms required to maintain data integrity. [source-ddd7b884997246d2]

Information engines require more than one memory state to leverage environmental correlations for work production, imposing a fundamental thermodynamic requirement for memory capacity. [peer-d7eafe8cadc2c1b84fdc3122]
notebooks.limitations: The synthesis connects distinct fields (theoretical information engines and practical DRAM hardware). The scaling laws between theoretical dissipation and hardware refresh power remain loosely defined.
notebooks.next_questions: How do refresh-induced dissipation rates in DRAM compare to the theoretical information-theoretic bounds for state retention?
notebooks.reason: Synthesis of existing sources to address the project objective for proj-thermo-mem-01.

proposal.summary: This research entry initiates an investigation into the physical implementation and thermodynamic costs of memory, specifically analyzing the trade-offs between retention, reliability, and free-energy consumption in stochastic systems. Building on the established causal state frameworks for information engines, we are pivoting to map how physical memories—beyond simple informational channels—incur costs through maintenance, switching, and erasure. By focusing on the thermodynamic cost of information storage and memory retention, we aim to delineate the relationship between predictive utility (the ability of a memory state to inform future control actions) and the energetic dissipation required to maintain that state against corruption. support.explanation: This reference demonstrates that refresh power is a significant operational cost that can be mitigated by architectural changes like morphable ECC, implying an intrinsic link between reliability and power consumption.
support.passage: [29] C. Chou, P. Nair, and M. K. Qureshi, “Reducing Refresh Power in Mobile Devices with Morphable ECC, ” inDSN, 2015.

review.alternative: Work production could be optimized without distinct memory states if the environment is static.
review.would_change_mind: Demonstration of an information engine producing work without memory states.

claims.statement: Information engines require more than one memory state to leverage environmental correlations for work production, imposing a fundamental thermodynamic requirement for memory capacity.

support.explanation: This establishes a theoretical necessity for memory states in work-producing processes, distinct from mere storage.
support.passage: The expression establishes that an information engine must have more than one memory state in order to leverage input environment correlations.
